implementation_notes: zio-kafka models the broker transaction as an effect: TransactionalProducer.make(TransactionalProducerSettings(producerSettings, transactionalId), consumer) produces a transactional producer whose createTransaction runs inside a ZIO Scope and commits when the scope closes, while produceChunkBatch receives the consumed offsets so records and offsets commit together. Consumers must use withReadCommitted(true) and the consumer stream must keep rebalance-safe commits enabled, since the producer depends on the consumer to hold up rebalances until the transaction completes.
pitfalls: A transaction interrupted before the scope closes is aborted: mark the scoped block uninterruptible or the commit is lost during shutdown.
Consumers without read_committed see records from uncommitted transactions, which defeats the atomicity the producer just paid for; rebalances must also hold offsets.
mapZIO collapses the stream chunks to single elements and destroys batching - use mapChunksZIO so records and offsets stay aligned.

variants.name: Alpakka / Pekko Connectors Kafka transactional stream
variants.implementation_notes: The streams realization wraps the transaction in the graph: Transactional.source materialises a transaction per element with the consumed offsets attached, Transactional.sink covers produce-only flows, and Transactional.flow passes a CommittableOffset through so downstream stages see only committed positions; commits happen when the stage completes and the graph is torn down. Use it when the pipeline is already an Akka or Pekko Streams graph; the maintained fork of Alpakka Kafka lives in Apache Pekko Connectors.
pitfalls: Transactional.flow must be driven by an offset-carrying source; mixing a plain Kafka source in front of it breaks the commit bookkeeping.
An abrupt stream failure aborts the transaction, so restart strategies (RestartSource) belong in the design instead of relying on consumer redelivery.
A second, non-transactional sink wired into the same graph escapes the transaction and reintroduces the dual write.
